text:
B: Hiya. Can you hear me alright?
A: Yeah. Hiya.
B: Dean. Tipton.
A: Liam. Walsall. Bloxwich.
B: Ar, not far then. Practically neighbours.
A: Yeah. I clocked the shirt on your photo.
B: [laughs] Albion. Me dad's fault. You?
A: Walsall. Loosely.
B: Oh, right. How'd they get on Saturday?
A: Drew. Again. They always draw.
B: Could be worse. Could be us at home to anybody.
A: Yeah.
B: What do you do then?
A: IT at a parcel depot. Junction ten. Scanners, printers, the Wi-Fi, all that. Just come off nights, so I'm a bit dead.
B: Ar, I know the feeling. I'm on lates this week. Press operator, Wednesbury. Brackets and that, for cars.
A: Long shifts?
B: Eight hours, days and lates. Bit of overtime when it's going. You?
A: Twelves. Fifty-odd hours, with the overtime. Pays alright.
B: Fifty hours. I couldn't do that, me. I'd be asleep at the press.
A: Energy drinks. Too many of them, to be honest.
B: [laughs] Yeah. The bacon bap van outside ours has gone up to four quid now. Four quid for a bap.
A: Four? That's taking the mick. There's a van by ours, three-fifty, sausage and egg.
B: Might have to come up yours for breakfast.
A: Yeah.
B: What do you do on your days off, then?
A: Er, build PCs, mostly. I buy broken stuff off Marketplace, fix it, sell it on. Got a graphics card last week, bloke wanted ninety quid for it cause the fan was dead, he thought the whole thing was knackered. Put a new fan on it, fiver, and I'll get two-fifty for it easy. Did a PS5 controller the week before, stick drift, that's just a little part, ten minutes with the soldering iron.
B: Stick drift? I've got that. On me controller. Call of Duty, I keep walking off to the left.
A: Yeah, that's the stick. Easy fix. Give it me and I'll do it.
B: Serious?
A: Tipton's ten minutes away. Tenner, for the part.
B: Ar, go on then. Do you play?
A: Yeah, shooters. Mic off though.
B: Same. Too many kids screaming at you.
A: Yeah. What else you do?
B: Fishing, mostly. Canal, or there's a pool up near Himley. Had a fourteen-pound carp last Sunday. The woman before, on the last call, couldn't believe I put it back.
A: [laughs] Yeah, I don't get it either.
B: It's just the quiet, really. Nobody on at you. Sat there with a flask. Kayleigh's got Ruby, it's the only time nobody wants nothing off me, do you know what I mean.
A: I walk the dog for that. Diesel. Staffie cross. Reedswood Park, early, after nights.
B: Ar, nice. Is he alright?
A: He's chewed the settee cushion again. Third one.
B: [laughs] Ruby wants a dog. I keep saying no.
A: Keep saying no.
B: Ar.
A: You doing the survey stuff properly after?
B: Yeah, sort of. I just click what feels right, you know.
A: Same. Just here for the money, me.
B: [laughs] Ar, same. Kayleigh said get the—
